info.bio:
Grupo de chicas de la decada de 1960 de la ciudad de Nueva York, conocidas en especial por su trabajo con Phil Spector. La formación de la banda estaba compuesta por Veronica Bennett en la voz principal, quien luego tomo el nombre de Ronnie Spector, su hermana Estelle Bennet y su prima Nedra Talley. Entre sus temas más populares destacan "Be My Baby", "Baby I Love You", "(The Best Part Of) Breakin' Up" y "(Walking) in the Rain". 

Después de un receso en el medio de la decada de los 60's

scenes.name: El soul conquista Gran Bretaña
scenes.author: Jon Savage
scenes.desc: El 26 de octubre «Reach Out I’ll Be There» de los Four Tops, con la flauta de aire oriental, el fraseo dylaniano de Lamont Dozier y la interpretación de su vida de Levi Stubbs, desbancó a «Distant Drums» y fue número 1: el momento en que la música negra americana ocupó el centro de la cultura juvenil británica, al revés que en el boom del beat. Lo habían preparado durante años los entusiastas: Dave Godin, que fundó en 1963 la Tamla Motown Appreciation Society, viajó a Detroit, llevó «Where Did Our Love Go» a los piratas y bautizó el sello Tamla Motown (marzo de 1965, con una gira de la revista que fracasó fuera de Londres); Guy Stevens, que pinchaba discos negros en el Scene y dirigió Sue Records para Chris Blackwell; Roger Eagle en el Twisted Wheel de Mánchester; Tony Hall promocionando Atlantic («In the Midnight Hour», el «My Girl» de Otis Redding); el DJ Jeff Dexter mezclando soul y ska en Tiles, el club subterráneo de Oxford Street del mod de masas que visitó Tom Wolfe. En otoño de 1966 Atlantic y Motown copaban las listas; Otis Redding metió a 8.000 personas en Tiles; los Four Tops arrasaron en el Savile de Brian Epstein el 13 de noviembre. El racismo, aun así, seguía ahí.

podcast.title: 1963 New Year's Resolution
podcast.body: Despite their popularity on stage and the backing of DJ Murray the K, The Ronettes' records on Colpix were not selling. Believing the label was the problem, they resolved in 1963 to seek out Phil Spector to produce them, given his growing reputation as a hitmaker. "They were going to get Phil Specter to produce them."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 110: "Be My Baby" by the Ronettes

podcast.title: 1964 UK Tour and Relationships
podcast.body: During a brief tour of the UK in early 1964, The Ronettes developed friendships with both The Beatles and their support act, The Rolling Stones. Ronnie experienced a "brief chaste flirtation" with John Lennon, while Estelle had a "little more" with George Harrison. Phil Spector even sent a telegram attempting to forbid The Rolling Stones from spending time with the group. "Soon after this, the group travelled to the UK for a brief tour in early 1964, drawing which they became friendly with the Beatles, Ronnie had a brief chaste flirtation with John Lennon, and Estelle something a little more with George Harrison."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 110: "Be My Baby" by the Ronettes

podcast.title: 1966 Beatles Tour Invitation and Substitute
podcast.body: In 1966, The Ronettes were invited to be the support act for The Beatles' last-ever tour. Phil Spector once again prevented Ronnie from participating, insisting she needed to be in the studio, leading to Elaine substituting for her, much to The Beatles' disappointment. No material from these studio sessions was ever released. "Also in 1966, the Runettes were invited by the Beatles to be their support act on their last ever tour, but once again Spectre insisted that Ronnie couldn't go because she needed to be in the studio, so Elaine substituted for her again..."

podcast.title: Group Disbandment (1967)
podcast.body: The Ronettes officially broke up in 1967, following a period of declining commercial success and Phil Spector's increasing control over Ronnie's career. "The group broke up in 1967..."

podcast.title: President Clinton's Fan Moment (1997)
podcast.body: Despite their early singles on Colpix Records being commercially unsuccessful, Ronnie Spector met President Clinton in 1997, who specifically requested she sign an album of those initial recordings. "when Ronnie met President Clinton in 1997, he asked her to sign a record, and specifically got her to sign an album of those early recordings for Colpix."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 110: "Be My Baby" by the Ronettes

podcast.title: Royalty Lawsuit (1998-2002)
podcast.body: In 1998, The Ronettes initiated a lawsuit against Phil Spector for unpaid royalties, having collectively received only $14,482.30 from all their hit records, an amount equivalent to a single 1964 royalty payment. Spector counter-argued he was owed money due to recording costs. After multiple appeals, each group member eventually received approximately $500,000 in 2002, which was still considered a small fraction of their true earnings. "By 1998, when the Vanette finally sued Specter for unpaid royalties, they had earned between them a total of $14,482.30 in royalties from all their hit records, the amount that came from a single 1964 royalty payment."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 110: "Be My Baby" by the Ronettes

podcast.title: Rock and Roll Hall of Fame Induction (2007)
podcast.body: Phil Spector, while a board member of the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, intentionally blocked The Ronettes' induction out of spite towards Ronnie. They were finally recognized and inducted into the Hall of Fame in 2007, after Spector had been imprisoned. "Specter, who was on the board of the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, prevented the Vanette from being inducted out of spite towards his ex until he was imprisoned, at which point they were finally recognised in 2007."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 110: "Be My Baby" by the Ronettes

podcast.title: Accidental Peppermint Lounge Gig
podcast.body: To circumvent age restrictions at the Peppermint Lounge during the height of the Twist craze, the underage girls dressed alike to appear older. The club manager mistook them for booked dancers who hadn't arrived, instructing them to perform, which inadvertently secured them a regular gig dancing behind Joey Dee and the Starliters. "As they were all dressed the same, the club's manager assumed they were the dancers he'd booked, who hadn't shown up."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 110: "Be My Baby" by the Ronettes

podcast.title: Auditioning for Phil Spector
podcast.body: Ronnie directly called Philles Records to reach Phil Spector, who surprisingly agreed to talk to her, revealing he was familiar with their Brooklyn Fox performances. At their audition, Spector stopped Ronnie during her rendition of "Why Do Fools Fall in Love," declaring, "That is the voice I've been looking for." "It only took her getting to the second line of the song before spec the elder to stop. That is the voice I've been looking for."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 110: "Be My Baby" by the Ronettes

podcast.title: Developing Signature Look
podcast.body: Performing at the Brooklyn Fox Theatre, The Ronettes developed their iconic and highly popular look, which included huge hair piled high, heavy mascara, and tight skirts designed to show off their legs. This style was inspired by street fashion, distinct from other girl groups of the era. "It was at these shows as well that they developed the look that they would become famous with, huge hair piled up on top of their heads, tons of mascara, and tight skirts lit to show their legs."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 110: "Be My Baby" by the Ronettes

podcast.title: Early 60s Chart Dominance
podcast.body: The Ronettes were part of the early 1960s heyday of girl groups, commanding the charts during this period. "when vocal ensembles like the charelles, the Ronets, and the Shangri-La's were commanding the charts."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
srcs.episode: Be My Baby-Baby-Baby Edition Part 2

podcast.title: Elaine Substitutes for Ronnie on Tour
podcast.body: After "Be My Baby" became a hit, The Ronettes were invited on Dick Clark's Caravan of Stars tour. However, Phil Spector insisted Ronnie remain in California to record the follow-up, so her cousin Elaine filled in for the first few weeks of the tour. Ronnie later realized this was Spector's deliberate attempt to isolate her from the group and her family. "so the girls' cousin Elaine filled in for her for the first couple of weeks of the tour, while Ronnie recorded another Barry, Greenwich and Spectre song, Baby I Love You."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 110: "Be My Baby" by the Ronettes

podcast.title: Florida Segregation Experience
podcast.body: While performing at a second Peppermint Lounge venue in Florida with Joey Dee and the Starliters, The Ronettes, as light-skinned mixed-race women, were mistakenly treated as "tanned white women" and served in restaurants that subsequently refused service to their darker-skinned mothers, exposing them firsthand to the realities of segregation. "That trip to Florida gave them two very different experiences. The first was that they got to see segregation first hand for the first time, and they didn't like it..."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 110: "Be My Baby" by the Ronettes

podcast.title: Followers of The Shirelles' Template
podcast.body: The Ronettes are listed as one of the prominent girl groups that followed in the footsteps of The Shirelles, who set the template for the booming girl group sound of the 1960s. "The Supremes, the Marvelettes, the crystals, the Ronettes, and the rest, all were following in the Chirrells footsteps."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 89: "Will You Love Me Tomorrow?" by the Shirelles

podcast.title: Meeting Murray the K
podcast.body: During their Florida trip, The Ronettes met Murray the K, New York's most popular DJ, who was impressed by their dancing. He offered them a performing spot on his regular shows at the Brooklyn Fox Theatre, which they eagerly accepted, being New York residents themselves. "Murray was down in Florida for a holiday, and was impressed enough by the girls dancing that he told them if they were ever in New York, and wanted a spot on one of his regular shows at the Brooklyn Fox Theatre, they should let him know."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 110: "Be My Baby" by the Ronettes

podcast.title: Name Change to The Ronettes
podcast.body: Inspired by other girl groups like The Bobbettes and The Marvelettes, Ronnie and her mother suggested changing the group's name from "Ronnie and the Relatives" to "Ron-Dettes," which they then shortened to The Ronettes. "Inspired by the Bobette and the Marvelette, Ronnie and her star's mother suggested changing the group's name. She suggested the run-debt, and they dropped the day, becoming the run-ette."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 110: "Be My Baby" by the Ronettes

podcast.title: Origin as Ronnie and the Relatives
podcast.body: The group began when Ronnie Bennett, inspired by Frankie Lymon, formed a vocal group with friends and relatives. At their debut at a Harlem Apollo talent show, the male lead singer suffered stage fright, prompting Ronnie to step forward and take over the lead vocal, impressing the notoriously hostile audience and leading to the formation of a smaller, regular performing group. "Ronnie stepped forward and took over the lead vocal, and the group went down well enough, even with the Apollo's notoriously hostile audience, that a smaller group of them decided to start performing regularly together."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 110: "Be My Baby" by the Ronettes

podcast.title: Origin at The Peppermint Lounge
podcast.body: Prior to becoming The Ronettes, the group, then known as Ronnie and the Relatives, made their initial appearances at The Peppermint Lounge. They performed backing vocals and danced behind Joey D and the Starlighters, who were the house band at the time. "And a tree oak called Ronnie and the Relatives made their first appearances at the Peppermint Lounge, singing backing vocals and dancing behind the Starlighters. They later changed their name to the Ronettes."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 91: "The Twist" by Chubby Checker

podcast.title: Rock and Roll Hall of Fame Inductee
podcast.body: This girl group is an inductee of the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, in contrast to The Pointer Sisters who have never been nominated. "The pointer sisters do not enjoy the same status as such rock and roll hall of fame inducted girl groups as Martha and the Vandela's, The Ronets..."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
srcs.episode: Yes We Can Can Edition Part 1

podcast.title: Ronnie's Impromptu Peppermint Lounge Vocal
podcast.body: During their accidental gig at the Peppermint Lounge, when Joey Dee and the Starliters played "What Did I Say"—a favorite of Ronnie's—she danced closely with lead singer David Pregati, who then handed her the microphone as a joke, and she took over the song, solidifying their regular performance spot. "He handed her the mic as a joke, and she took over the song."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 110: "Be My Baby" by the Ronettes

podcast.title: Spector Sabotaging Career
podcast.body: As Phil Spector became increasingly erratic and controlling, he recorded numerous "great records" with The Ronettes but inexplicably refused to release them, claiming they weren't "quite right." Ronnie later understood this was likely a deliberate strategy to sabotage their career and keep her exclusively to himself. "he recorded many great records with the Runette, which he refused to release, claiming they weren't quite right. Ronnie has later realised that he was probably trying to sabotage their career, so he could have her all to himself..."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 110: "Be My Baby" by the Ronettes

podcast.title: Spector's Concealed Marriage
podcast.body: While working with Phil Spector, Ronnie became romantically involved with him. During a writing session at his apartment, she discovered women's shoes and, upon asking, Spector falsely claimed they belonged to his sister, concealing his marital status. "Spectre hadn't told her he was married, and claimed to her when she asked that they belong to his sister."
